title: SensAiry (Eddystone)
notes: How the SensAiry app (com.tymtix.sensairy 2.10.07, read for interoperability on 2026-11-18) reads its 'classic' external sensors: an Eddystone-UID frame, service data under UUID FEAA with frame type 00. Data: A frame type, B tx power, C-L namespace (10 bytes), M-R instance (6 bytes). Instance bytes 0-1 as a big-endian short shifted right by 5 is kPa (the app shows it in psi after dividing by 6.89576 and subtracting an altitude correction, 14.7*((293-0.0065*altitude_m)/293)^5.2558 - 14.54, about 0.16 psi at sea level; readings below 3.9 psi show as 0). Instance byte 2 is the temperature as a signed byte in degC. The low 4 bits of instance byte 1 are flags. Namespace bytes 2 and 3 are the firmware version. The app tells sensors apart by Bluetooth address; whether the namespace identifies a sensor is a guess (sensorId), to be checked against a capture. Marked 'inferred' until a capture from the car matches the app's readings.
